title: Casper and the Ledger
premise: In 1893, on a storm-battered coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Rafael Marchetti keeps the town's ledger of names — debts, births, grudges — believing history belongs to bigger places. When the army requisitions the harbor town to build fortifications, an officer seizes the ledger as evidence of 'irregular obligations,' threatening families with eviction and conscription. Rafael discovers his late wife's name appears in pages he never wrote, tying him to a smuggling network that fed the poor for decades. To save the town, he must reconstruct the true ledger in the old chandlery workshop before the requisition ship sails on the morning tide — and choose between the law's version of justice and the one written by ordinary hands. He finishes at dawn, trades himself for the town's names, and finds belonging not in keeping records but in being kept by them.
about_author: Rosalind Okafor is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing maritime court records from coastal garrisons, where she first encountered ledgers seized as evidence. She writes historical fiction about the paperwork of power and the people it was never meant to describe.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Rafael tends the light and updates the town ledger, a duty inherited from his wife Elena. POV: Rafael. Establishes his grief, his belief that history happens elsewhere, and the ledger's quiet authority over the harbor town.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Warships appear at dawn; an advance officer posts requisition notices. Fisherman Tomás begs Rafael to hide certain pages. POV: Rafael. The intrusion of history arrives literally on the tide, shattering his sense of distance.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Captain Aldous Vane occupies the town hall and demands all civic records. The council surrenders the ledger; Rafael watches his wife's handwriting carried off like contraband. POV: Rafael. First confrontation with Vane's cold legality.

chapters.title: What Elena Kept
chapters.summary: Rummaging the lighthouse storeroom, Rafael finds Elena's duplicate entries — names, sums, deliveries of grain marked only with a gull symbol. POV: Rafael, with a flashback to Elena. He realizes she ran something larger than bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Gull Mark
chapters.summary: Rafael confronts old Widow Ferran, who admits the gull mark fed families during the famine years — a smuggling ring Elena coordinated. POV: Rafael then Ferran. Belonging revealed as something he was inside without knowing.

chapters.title: Vane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vane begins prosecuting 'irregular obligations' from the seized ledger; three families face eviction, two sons face conscription. POV: Vane. Humanizes him as a man who genuinely believes order is mercy.

chapters.title: Eviction at Number Nine
chapters.summary: Soldiers evict the Okonkwo family; the town watches, cowed. Rafael nearly intervenes but holds back, ashamed. POV: Rafael. His passivity becomes unbearable to himself.

chapters.title: The Chandlery Still Stands
chapters.summary: Ferran shows Rafael the abandoned chandlery workshop where Elena worked — presses, paper, ink, and half a forged second ledger already begun. POV: Rafael. Hope kindles: finish the true record before the army ships out.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Rafael learns the requisition ship departs on the morning tide in fourteen days, taking the ledger and the condemned men with it. A deadline is set. POV: Rafael. The clock starts.

chapters.title: Ink and Salt Air
chapters.summary: Rafael begins reconstructing entries from memory, testimony, and Elena's duplicates; the workshop becomes a refuge where townsfolk bring their own accounts. POV: rotating townsfolk vignettes. Community coheres around the work.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Someone reports suspicious lamplight at the chandlery; Vane raids it and finds nothing but rope and tar — the ledger hidden in the salt cellar. But suspicion now has a face. POV: Vane and Rafael. Paranoia enters the town.

chapters.title: Tomás's Confession
chapters.summary: Tomás admits he informed, coerced by threats against his son. Rafael must forgive or lose his crew. POV: Tomás. Betrayal reframed as survival under occupation.

chapters.title: Elena's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Decoding Elena's cipher, Rafael finds her final entry: a warning that Vane's predecessor took bribes, and proof hidden beneath the lighthouse. POV: Rafael. The personal grief becomes political ammunition.

chapters.title: Beneath the Light
chapters.summary: Rafael excavates the lighthouse foundation during a storm watch and recovers letters implicating the colonial administration. POV: Rafael. He risks the light itself — the town's safety — for the truth.

chapters.title: A Dark Night
chapters.summary: With the lamp unattended, a fishing boat founders; sailors drown. The town turns on Rafael. POV: Rafael and survivor Marta. His crusade exacts its first terrible price.

chapters.title: Vane Offers Terms
chapters.summary: Vane, shaken by the wreck, offers Rafael a deal: surrender the evidence, and the evictions stop. Rafael sees the trap — the names would still sail. POV: both. Justice outside the law versus mercy within it.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: Rafael lays everything before the townsfolk in the church cellar: finish the ledger and risk everything, or take Vane's terms. They vote to finish. POV: ensemble. Belonging becomes a choice made aloud.

chapters.title: Three Nights' Work
chapters.summary: A race against discovery: scribes work in shifts while soldiers patrol; Ferran decoys a search party; the last pages are pressed and bound. POV: rapid ensemble cuts. Rising tension toward the climax.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Vane, tipped by a second informer, storms the chandlery at midnight. In the struggle the original seized ledger burns; Vane realizes his evidence is gone and only Rafael's reconstruction remains. POV: Rafael and Vane. Climax begins.

chapters.title: Trade at the Quay
chapters.summary: At dawn, Rafael walks onto the quay and offers himself and the finished ledger in exchange for the town's names struck from the requisition rolls. Vane, unable to prove anything else, accepts. POV: Rafael. The sacrifice.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Rafael, detained aboard, watches the ship carry him away — until naval auditors, summoned by mailed copies of the evidence, halt departure and arrest Vane instead. POV: Rafael. Justice arrives sideways, through the work itself.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Hand
chapters.summary: Months later, the town restores the chandlery as a reading room; the reconstructed ledger rests open under glass, Elena's gull mark stamped on its cover. Rafael lights the lamp each night, no longer a bystander to history. POV: Rafael. Resolution: inheritance accepted, belonging earned.
